pageCache.pageTitle: Gatehouse School | Independent non-selective school in London for Girls & BoysGatehouse School | Independent non-selective school in London for Girls & Boys
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Gatehouse School
Gatehouse is an independent school for girls and boys aged 3 to 11 in East London, near Victoria Park.
Accommodated in a recently renovated Victorian building with modern extensions and set in landscaped grounds which include climbing frames and an Astroturf sports court. The site is alongside Regent’s Canal and the many acres of Victoria Park.
At Gatehouse we aim to provide children with a caring and supportive learning environment, developing and encouraging each child’s abilities and helping them to build an excellent foundation for life and work. Classes are non-streamed, and of mixed ability throughout all age ranges.
From the nursery and onwards, children are subject taught by highly qualified specialist staff as well as having their own dedicated form teacher.

pageCache.pageTitle: Drama | Independent School, East London | Gatehouse SchoolDrama | Independent School, East London | Gatehouse School
pageCache.text:
At Gatehouse School, Drama and Performance are an integral part of our curriculum and school culture. From Nursery to Year 6, pupils develop creativity, confidence and communication skills through a wide range of opportunities to rehearse, perform and express themselves.
Drama Linked to the Curriculum
Drama lessons are closely linked to each year group’s English curriculum, enhancing learning through role play, storytelling and character exploration. While not every session leads to a final performance, lessons are carefully designed to:
Build confidence in public speaking
Strengthen teamwork and active listening
Encourage empathy and imagination
Introduce theatre styles and history
Promote learning through creative play
A Stage for Every Pupil
From the earliest years, Gatehouse pupils rehearse and perform in our purpose-built Wallbank Hall, making use of professional lighting and sound systems. Each class presents at least one whole-school assembly per year, often sharing their learning from PSHE in imaginative ways.
A Year-Round Performance Calendar
Our performance calendar gives all pupils the chance to shine and build their stagecraft across the year:
Annual Poetry Competition
Year 4 Poetry Performance Project (featuring limericks, kennings, haikus and more)
ISA Shakespeare Monologue Competition
Year 2 Musical Theatre Production
Gatehouse’s Got Talent!
Year 6 Musical Production
LAMDA Tuition and Examinations
From Year 3 onwards, pupils may opt to take LAMDA Communication and Performance tuition, working towards graded group acting exams. These sessions help pupils develop:
Confidence in spoken word
Interpretation and performance skills
A love of literature and drama
Clear, expressive communication
More Than Performance
At Gatehouse, Drama and Performance are more than just shows and scripts. They are a key part of developing articulate, empathetic, and self-assured learners who are ready to express themselves and connect with others.

pageCache.pageTitle: Music | Co-educational Prep School, London | Gatehouse SchoolMusic | Co-educational Prep School, London | Gatehouse School
pageCache.text:
Music is a high-profile and valued part of life at Gatehouse. Every pupil receives a weekly class music lesson and has the opportunity to explore and enjoy music through a wide range of activities and clubs.
Co-Curricular Opportunities
Beyond classroom learning, pupils are encouraged to join the many musical groups available at Gatehouse, including:
These are led by the Head of Music and a team of skilled peripatetic instrumental teachers.
Orchestras
Ukulele groups
Brass ensembles
Performance Opportunities
Performance is an important part of music at Gatehouse, pupils have the opportunity to take part in several performances throughout the year. These may include:
Nursery Nativity plays
Christmas concerts
Solo instrumental performances in assembly
Year 2 and Year 6 musicals
Ensemble and choral concerts held each term
Individual Instrumental Tuition – FAQs
What instruments can my child learn?
We offer a broad range of instrumental tuition delivered by specialist teachers during the school day. Lessons currently available include:
Drum kit
Clarinet
Saxophone
Recorder
French horn
Orchestral percussion
When does tuition take place?
Lessons take place during school hours and are 30 minutes long. They are scheduled on a weekly rota to ensure that pupils do not miss the same subject lesson each week.
Can my child take music exams?
Yes. Pupils who learn a musical instrument at school may choose to take ABRSM Grade Exams. These are held at Gatehouse each term and are entirely optional. Our peripatetic instrumental teachers, in coordination with the Head of Music, will advise and support pupils as they progress and prepare for exams. Further information about ABRSM exams can be found on their website.
How do I arrange music lessons for my child?
The school will help arrange an introduction with an appropriate music teacher. The teacher will provide details on availability, costs, and any terms and conditions. Payment is made directly to the teacher, and lessons are typically invoiced in blocks of ten per term (though this may vary slightly).
What notice is needed to stop lessons?
Should you wish to discontinue individual music lessons, a half-term’s written notice is required.

pageCache.pageTitle: Reception Curriculum | Preparatory School | Gatehouse SchoolReception Curriculum | Preparatory School | Gatehouse School
pageCache.text:
Reception is the final year of the Early Years Foundation Stage and our pupils continue to follow the Foundation Stage Profile which incorporates all seven areas of learning. There is a clear progression from Nursery in that the children learn through play and investigation, but more formally supported and scaffolded by the teacher. As in Nursery, Reports and Parents’ Evenings take place in the Autumn and Summer terms.
Once in Reception, the daily individual reading sessions begin. Every child at Gatehouse School has their progress tracked by the use of a reading log which is sent home daily. Homework also starts in Reception and is sent by email at the start of every half term. This gives parents an insight into the week’s learning objective.
At Gatehouse School all pupils are given opportunities to participate in both indoor and outdoor learning. This is made extremely easy with our new outdoor learning terraces which are accessed from each Reception class providing endless possibilities for child initiated learning through free-flow play and investigation.
Pupils at Gatehouse School have weekly swimming lessons which are taught in small groups at York Hall Swimming Baths in Bethnal Green, equipping each pupil with this essential life-skill.

pageCache.text:
At Gatehouse School, we strongly believe that learning a foreign language provides valuable educational, social, and cultural experiences for our pupils. It prepares them to thrive in a rapidly changing world, where communication and collaboration often take place in languages other than English.
Our French Curriculum
French is taught from the Early Years Foundation Stage and continues throughout the school, with structured progression in Key Stage 2. This early introduction helps lay a strong foundation for future language learning, developing both confidence and curiosity.
Our French programme aligns with the National Languages Strategy, which states that: “Every child should have the opportunity to study a foreign language and develop their interest in the culture of other nations.”
Enjoyment and enthusiasm for learning a new language
Practical communication skills using listening, speaking, reading, and writing
Confidence and spontaneity in using French in real-world contexts
Awareness and appreciation of other cultures and ways of life
Enrichment Opportunities
Language learning at Gatehouse goes beyond the classroom. Pupils enjoy a variety of cultural and immersive experiences that bring the French language to life:
Year 5 Residential Trip to the Opal Coast, France – a three-day visit offering real-world language use and cultural exploration
Visits to the French Institute, South Kensington – enhancing cultural understanding through films and exhibitions
European Day of Languages – celebrated in collaboration with other schools, such as Blackheath High School

pageCache.pageTitle: Celebrating Our Eco Partnership | Gatehouse SchoolCelebrating Our Eco Partnership | Gatehouse School
pageCache.text:
Celebrating Our Eco Partnership with TRIBE Hotel Canary Wharf
We are delighted to continue our valued partnership with TRIBE Hotel in Canary Wharf, who have been proudly supporting our eco projects since 2023. This collaboration has become an important part of our school’s commitment to sustainability, offering our pupils meaningful, real-world insight into environmentally responsible practices.
TRIBE is part of Ennismore, a creative hospitality company rooted in culture and community, with a global collective of entrepreneurial and founder-built brands with purpose at their heart. This shared focus on purpose and responsibility aligns closely with our school values and enhances the impact of our partnership.
Each year, the TRIBE team visits us on World Environment Day to lead engaging and inspiring assemblies. These sessions give our children the opportunity to learn about the sustainable choices made within the hotel industry, helping them to understand how businesses can play a key role in protecting our planet.
This year, to celebrate Earth Day, TRIBE Hotel has launched an exciting whole-school eco poster competition. Following a special video introduction from their team, our pupils have been enthusiastically designing and creating posters based on their favourite eco-friendly ideas. It has been wonderful to see their creativity and passion for sustainability come to life.
The competition offers a fantastic opportunity for our children to have their work showcased beyond the classroom. The five winning posters will be proudly displayed in the hotel lobby in Canary Wharf, allowing guests to see and celebrate the children’s efforts. To make the occasion even more special, the winners will also be invited to a celebratory pancake party in recognition of their achievements.
We are very much looking forward to welcoming TRIBE Hotel back on World Environment Day, when they will announce the competition winners. It promises to be a memorable moment for our school community, and we cannot wait to see all of the fantastic entries.
This partnership continues to inspire our pupils to think globally, act responsibly, and take pride in making a positive difference – values that sit at the heart of our school.

pageCache.text:
At Gatehouse, we aim to inspire and support every pupil to reach their full potential. We believe that all children, regardless of ability or attainment level, should have access to a rich and inclusive mathematics curriculum.
Our approach to teaching mathematics is designed to ensure that pupils develop not only strong foundational skills, but also the confidence and curiosity to explore mathematical ideas in depth.
Our Aims in Mathematics
At Gatehouse, we strive to:
Enrichment and Digital Learning
Upper Junior pupils have the opportunity to take part in national mathematics competitions, helping them to develop confidence, resilience, and a love of challenge beyond the classroom.
To support and enhance learning, we make use of a variety of high-quality digital platforms, including Mathletics, Atom Learning, and Times Table Rockstars. These tools offer personalised practice, support fluency, and allow children to consolidate and extend their mathematical understanding both in school and at home.

pageCache.pageTitle: Music | Independent Prep School | Gatehouse SchoolMusic | Independent Prep School | Gatehouse School
pageCache.text:
Gatehouse School believes strongly in encouraging an interest, understanding and above all a passion in all approaches to music.
Each week every class in the school from Nursery to Year 6 is taught in our dedicated music room with access to a wide variety of instruments, recording equipment and musical resources.
At Gatehouse School the children are taught music through units of work based on the concepts of listening, performing and composing. Children are able to develop team-working skills by participating in group composing activities, and enhance their note-reading skills when playing on the keyboard or tuned percussions. Children in Years 3 and 4 also take part in whole-class ukulele lessons.
Our pupils frequently enjoy concerts and workshops run by professional musicians from, amongst others, the LSO, the London Arts Orchestra and Tower Hamlets Arts and Music Education Service.
Here at Gatehouse School we are extremely proud of our range of extra-curricular musical ensembles for our children to be a part of. These include Years 3 – 6 Mixed Senior Choir, Mixed Chamber Choir, School Orchestra, Chamber Orchestra, Brass & Wind Ensembles and West African Drumming Group.
Our termly music concerts are important celebrations of the talent within the school, which also showcase the variety of choral and orchestral ensembles we are proud to have at Gatehouse School.

pageCache.pageTitle: Science | Co-educational School | Gatehouse SchoolScience | Co-educational School | Gatehouse School
pageCache.text:
From Nursery to Year 6, the Gatehouse Science provision is notable for its immersive and experiential approach to learning. The curriculum is designed to spark curiosity and enthusiasm in every child, inviting them to explore, engage, and experiment with the wonders of the world.
We empower students with the knowledge and skills to uncover nature’s marvels through stimulating inquiry and hands-on experiences. Children are encouraged to ask questions, make discoveries, and apply their understanding, helping them make meaningful connections to the world around them.
Teaching & Learning Approach
In our lessons, we adopt an enquiry-based approach that actively engages children in their learning process. Students learn to recognise the types of enquiry they are using—such as observational, comparative, or fair testing—and identify the scientific skills they are developing, including data collection and analysis.
By reflecting on and evaluating their experiments, children develop a cycle of enquiry that often leads to new questions and ideas for further investigation. This approach deepens their scientific understanding, nurtures inquisitiveness, and encourages critical thinking both inside and beyond the classroom.
Curriculum Coverage
Our curriculum is thoughtfully designed to cover a wide range of topics across biology, chemistry, and physics. Interactive and practical lessons are at the heart of our teaching, helping children to:
It is this engaging, hands-on approach that makes science at Gatehouse stand out.
Master key concepts in science.
Develop problem-solving and reasoning skills.
Build a genuine curiosity about the world.
Inclusive Provision & Differentiation
Every child excels within the science department because teaching is tailored to meet diverse needs, interests, and abilities. Through collaboration with the SEND department and Nurture teachers, we create an inclusive and effective learning environment.
Our strategies include:
This ensures that all students, regardless of learning preference, are able to access and enjoy science.
Direct instruction and step-by-step guidance.
Hands-on activities and visual aids.
Technology to break down complex concepts.
Guided questioning and supportive feedback.
Facilities
Our commitment to outstanding science education is reinforced by our well-equipped laboratory. Here, students have the opportunity to take part in memorable practical work—from using Bunsen burners to conducting heart and eye dissections – bringing scientific concepts to life in a fun, engaging, and meaningful way.
Opportunities Beyond the Classroom
Clubs & Competitions
To extend learning beyond lessons, we offer a wide range of opportunities including:
STEAM Clubs (Science, Technology, Engineering, Art, Mathematics).
Gardening initiatives to link science with sustainability.
Special Events & Trips
STEAM Careers Links
We invite parents and visitors with careers in STEAM to share their experiences with pupils, offering valuable insights into professions and real-world applications of their learning. Children also conduct interviews with STEAM professionals, building awareness of the skills and pathways involved.
During lessons, we highlight how topics connect to future careers, nurturing aspirations and empowering students to imagine exciting futures in STEAM fields.
Environmental Commitment
We are dedicated to raising environmentally conscious citizens. Each class elects Eco Warriors, who meet weekly to discuss initiatives and review progress.
Through these initiatives, students learn that science is not only about discovery but also about making responsible choices for a better future.
Second-hand uniform sales to promote sustainability.
Celebrating Achievement
At Gatehouse, the science department celebrates every success, no matter how small. From classroom experiments to competitions and eco-initiatives, every child’s contribution is valued.
By fostering curiosity, creativity, and collaboration, we inspire pupils to explore the wonders of science, igniting a lifelong passion for discovery and empowering them to build bright futures.

pageCache.pageTitle: School History | Preparatory School, London | Gatehouse SchoolSchool History | Preparatory School, London | Gatehouse School
pageCache.text:
The Story of Gatehouse School
Gatehouse School began in 1860, when a school for 270 pupils was built in ecclesiastical style on Sewardstone Road with a grant from the National Society, funded by Parliament.
George Lansbury, who went on to become a British politician and Leader of the Opposition, attended the school from 1868 to 1870.
By 1898, the school had fallen into disrepair. John Edwin Watts-Ditchfield, vicar of St James the Less (and later the first Bishop of Chelmsford), sought support to restore the buildings. An anonymous donor offered to fund the repairs.
The foundation stone for the new parochial building was laid in 1899, and the new school officially opened on 29th June 1901.
War and Rebuilding
In 1908, the building was sold to the London County Council and served as a school for many years.
During World War I (1914–1918), a War Memorial was placed in the school to honour those who gave their lives. It was later moved during restoration works and now resides safely on an upper floor, where wreaths are placed each year.
In 1944, following the heavy bombing of East London, St James the Less Church was destroyed, and the school sustained significant damage. A historical bomb damage map shows the extent of destruction in the Bethnal Green area, including photographs of the damaged school interior.
A Montessori Legacy
In May 1948, Phyllis Wallbank MBE opened a small school in the Gatehouse of St Bartholomew the Great Priory Church, West Smithfield. The school’s ethos was rooted in the teaching of Maria Montessori.
Due to its popularity, the school moved to its current home on Sewardstone Road, Victoria Park. A memorable moment in the school’s history was Maria Montessori’s visit in 1951.
Phyllis Wallbank, pictured in the grounds of Gatehouse with her dog, remained a key figure in the school’s development. Sadly, she passed away in 2020, though her legacy lives on through the school, it’s mission, staff and pupils.
Read more about her life:
Biography at PWETRUST.org
The Telegraph Obituary
Gatehouse School Today
The building has seen many changes over the decades and now houses around 528 pupils aged 3 to 11.
With a strong sense of heritage and community, the Governors, staff, pupils and parents continue to look forward with pride and excitement as Gatehouse School moves confidently into the future.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome from the Headteacher | London | Gatehouse SchoolWelcome from the Headteacher | London | Gatehouse School
pageCache.text:
A warm welcome to the Gatehouse website, and thank you for expressing an interest in Gatehouse School. Our website will provide you with excellent insight into the friendly, family community that we are, and I do hope that you can gauge the positive energy, happiness and enthusiasm in all aspects of learning that makes Gatehouse such a special place to learn and grow.
As Headteacher of Gatehouse School I am proud of our non-selective, inclusive ethos, and I am supported by a dedicated and talented team of staff who ensure that each child’s natural curiosity about the world is encouraged and expanded. All of our successes are achieved through the successful blend of traditional values and modern educational principles.
Staying true to the vision of our founder, Mrs Phyllis Wallbank, all children at Gatehouse School are valued as individuals and they develop an excellent approach to academic work, achieving high standards throughout the school during their time with us. Our positive and personalised approach to teaching and learning ensures that all of our children acquire a determination and enthusiasm to enjoy every opportunity, and that they learn to try their best in all that they do.
As a parent myself I appreciate how choosing the right school for your child is one of the most important decisions that you can make on their behalf. You will be entrusting into our care your most treasured possession and we are committed to ensuring that a successful partnership enables your child to achieve in all areas of development. I warmly welcome you to visit our school where you will see for yourselves how your child will thrive and achieve at Gatehouse School.
I do hope to have the opportunity to meet with you as soon as possible.

pageCache.pageTitle: Year 2 Curriculum | Independent School | Gatehouse SchoolYear 2 Curriculum | Independent School | Gatehouse School
pageCache.text:
Year 2 is the final Year of Lower Juniors before our pupils make the important transition into our subject taught curriculum in the Upper Juniors. Throughout this time, children are prepared and taught how to be independent and confident learners.
As in Year 1, children continue to be taught by their form teacher who is responsible for the following subjects: maths, English, science, history, geography and PSHE. Children receive specialist teaching in ICT, French, music, art and PE.
The children read to a member of staff at Gatehouse School three to four times a week and are encouraged to read a range of genres. Reading is reinforced through the children’s weekly library lesson in our new, bright, well stocked Library.
In Year 2 we enable our pupils to consolidate and broaden their learning skills and abilities through creative and stimulating lessons. Our topics vary from studying traditional stories to the history of food, weather, poetry linked to the five senses as well as the Great Fire of London.
Homework is set daily and covers all form subjects in addition to reading and spelling.
At the end of Year 2 our pupils at Gatehouse are ready for their seamless progression into our Upper Juniors department.

pageCache.text:
Nursery & Reception Children – Local Authority Nursery Funding
15 hours per week funding (term time)
At present this is available to all children up to and including the term in which they reach five years of age and covers the first 15 hours per week. We will apply for this funding on your behalf. This will be reflected on the invoice you receive from us in each term when the funding applies.
Please note that this funding is dependent upon government legislation and the policies of the London Borough of Tower Hamlets and the situation could change at short notice. If funding is withdrawn, for any reason, then parents are still liable for the full school fee as published by the School.
